text:
claire_dev: hitting a weird SSL verify failure with the Python async SDK when targeting Dedicated/private endpoints behind a local sidecar proxy + custom CA. curl with --cacert works but httpx inside our sample app fails. :thinking:

claire_dev: tiny repro (async):
```py
from redwood import AsyncClient
client = AsyncClient(base_url="https://private.internal:8443", api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_KEY'])
await client.chat.create("ping")
```

claire_dev: in the container /etc/ssl/custom-ca.pem is mounted. `curl --cacert /etc/ssl/custom-ca.pem https://private.internal:8443/health` -> 200. httpx raises `ssl.SSLError: [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed`.

ben_platform: common culprits: httpx's trust_env interaction with HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY and httpx's default SSLContext. try passing an explicit ssl.SSLContext that loads your CA and set trust_env=False.

ben_platform: quick workaround:
```py
import ssl
ssl_ctx = ssl.create_default_context()
ssl_ctx.load_verify_locations('/etc/ssl/custom-ca.pem')
client = AsyncClient(base_url='https://private.internal:8443', api_key=..., ssl=ssl_ctx, trust_env=False)
```

claire_dev: that bypasses the handshake error. follow-ups: 1) docs don't show ssl param or trust_env guidance, 2) our retry middleware retries on SSL errors which hides the root cause in logs (multiple retries then final failure).

maria_onboard: agree — onboarding only has a simple quickstart. propose adding a "Dedicated / Private: proxy + custom CA" snippet with the exact example and a docker-compose sample. include env vars: HTTP_PROXY, HTTPS_PROXY, REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE and note httpx honors trust_env.

ryan_sre: on retries: we currently consider transport exceptions retryable. ssl.SSLError that is a cert verification failure should be non-retryable. I'll open an issue to refine the retry predicate and improve logging to say "non-retryable SSL verification failure".

ben_platform: SDK changes I'll prepare: 1) accept ssl: Optional[ssl.SSLContext] on AsyncClient ctor and expose it in stubs, 2) type AsyncClient.__aenter__ to return the concrete client type in .pyi so context manager use is typed, 3) add unit test that simulates ssl.SSLError and verifies no retries.

claire_dev: I'll draft a docs PR with the repro and include both the httpx stacktrace and the successful curl line. will add example under examples/dedicated-proxy-ca with a tiny Dockerfile + compose.

deploy-bot: pushed branch feat/dedicated-proxy-ca-docs by claire_dev to staging/docs (CI queued) :rocket:

ben_platform: will open the SDK PR after the docs. also update typed stubs to include `ssl: Optional[ssl.SSLContext]` and make __aenter__ return "RedwoodAsyncClient" for better mypy UX.

ryan_sre: note for infra folks: env + sidecar (envoy/squid) combos are tricky. mounting the CA and providing an explicit ssl context or disabling trust_env is the pragmatic workaround in k8s.

maria_onboard: cc @docs for wording help. include a short checklist: mount CA, set REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE for sync requests, and for async httpx flows either pass ssl context or set trust_env=False.

claire_dev: thanks all — will link PRs back here when ready. saved us a lot of time. :tada:
